summary: multisample_pid.py charge --toys left out, without saying so, every toy event with a per-layer sample outside the response table, so the predicted core width came from the surviving toys only and was too narrow when the table ends inside the per-layer Landau tail at --toy-z.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the defective code is in the script as first released (hep-research 0.14.0, commit f7d5722d); the 0.14.0 release already held the file

observables: toy_prediction.sigma68, median, mean and tail_fraction of multisample_pid.py charge
impact.bias: the predicted width is biased low: in the audit's case (table ending at signal 4, toy Z 1.9, relative width 0.12, 4 layers, truncated mean 0.25) 7.5% of the toys were kept and sigma68 was 0.051 against 0.097 for all toys; a data width compared with it looked too wide
impact.trigger: --toys with truncated-mean or weighted-mean and a response table that does not cover the per-layer tail at --toy-z; toy_prediction.n below inputs.toys shows it

outputs.how_to_recognize: JSON on stdout of multisample_pid.py charge with a toy_prediction block (inputs.toys set) and a method other than likelihood; affected when the response table's highest signal lies inside the per-layer tail at --toy-z (toy_prediction.n below inputs.toys); outputs of the fixed version carry toy_prediction.toys_used

remedy: rerun multisample_pid.py charge with this version and read the warning and toy_prediction.toys_used; extend the response table past the per-layer tail at --toy-z so that no toy is left out
